html:
A series of wars from about 166 to 180 between Rome and peoples north of the Danube: mainly the Germanic Marcomanni and Quadi and the Sarmatian Iazyges.

They struck while the empire was weak from the Antonine Plague and a war with Parthia. Around 170 raiders broke through, besieged Aquileia and reached northern Italy, the first such invasion in centuries. Marcus Aurelius spent most of his last years in camps on the river, and wrote part of his Meditations there.

Rome won back the line, and Marcus may have planned new provinces beyond it. He died in 180 and his son Commodus made peace instead. The wars are shown on the Column of Marcus Aurelius in Rome. Many historians see them as an early sign of the pressure on the frontiers that grew in the third century.
sum: A series of wars from about 166 to 180 between Rome and peoples north of the Danube: mainly the Germanic Marcomanni and Quadi and the Sarmatian Iazyges.
